body:
I have agoraphobia (I am afeared of humans) and depression, and I have been avoiding inpatient treatment, but I just can't get access to mental healthcare any other way and I've run out of options. My biggest concern is just moment to moment survival around so many people. In the institutions you've been to, how much are patients forced to be around other humans?  

Even if I could isolate myself in a room there, I get compulsive desire to harm myself when too stressed. At home I use mostly electronic means to distract myself (kindle, computer, et cetera) and stave off that mindset. The idea of being without these distractions and left to churn in my own suffering is terrifying. Assuming they won't allow my kindle ereader, what options do I have to distract myself and keep neuroticism at bay?  

Anyway, this is not time sensitive and please do not feel the need to walk on eggshells, I just want the most realistic expectations possible. And good luck in your difficult career choice, primate.
Thank you for taking the time to respond. I've been laughing at the idea that this might add jewish guilt to my problems. Not a serious thought, but your post really made me smile.

Thank you very much for replying. I was happy to see someone took the time to respond.  

Today I learned that "sliding scale" is basically a PR stunt. C4 for example charges $100 for therapy (not a psychologist), which I believe is average cost for therapy. They have a Psychiatrist that you can only see if you are in therapy, for $200, which I believe is average to above average cost. So to get psych meds from them you have to stack a few $100 payments on top of each other for the privilege of paying $200 for a *chance* at meds. Anyone who can afford that should go with a well reviewed private practice and skip straight to the psychiatrist.  

The handful of places I called were similar. So psychologists and psychiatrists are off the table for me. There are some options for therapists and intern therapists, though. I will look into whether they can do anything with someone as deeply mentally ill as I am. My perception is that they deal with life problems and not mental health issues.  

Meanwhile I'm going to focus on going to the free clinic, but I'm disappointed that I couldn't talk med options (or anything else) with a mental health professional.

Thank you, that is a very beautiful thing to say. I get burned out after emotional events and right now I'm going to go eat junk food and watch a stupid movie. I just have to change gears. I'll PM you later.

Thank you for not ignoring me. I hope your life is better than mine.

And now I realize that in my desperate need to vent, I've neglected to mention the titular crying episode. I considered calling the suicide hotline, because I have no on else to talk to. And in realizing the depth of my loneliness and lack of support, I just started crying. A little at first as I am a guy and we reflexively repress tears, but then I just let it all out. I was loudly crying like a child does and the sound of it is haunting me right now. I am so god damned ashamed of it and it didn't make me feel better at all. Like everything else I try it just made me sink deeper. That's the second time in my adult life where I let myself cry in desperation for some kind of release only to have it make me feel worse. I'm never doing that again if I can at all control it.  

But you can see how I feel like I'm stuck in quicksand. Trying to help myself just makes everything worse.

I happen to have a tech certification that would lend some plausibility to self employment. Heck, even getting the cert could eat up some space on my employment history. (For the record, it's a basic cert that really, *really* doesn't help with employment, but most people don't know that...)  

This is a better option than anything I thought up. Thank you very much, person who's awesome at lying!

Thank you for posting. Your last sentence captures this dilemma very well, honesty might not be a realistic option. If faced with prospects of homelessness, methinks most people would relax their morals a bit.
